goal: Restore the shared terminal/KitCode Welcome setup UI from before the full per-OS skin pivot, while keeping OS detection and making only the header window controls platform-specific (macOS left traffic lights, Windows right controls, Linux-style header controls).

in: Keep resolveSetupPlatform() and pass platform from onboarding Electron into the renderer.
Restore one shared terminal Welcome body UI (monospace, red/green dark palette, tab/statusline composition, [x]/[ ] option marks) for darwin, win32, and linux.
Keep OS-specific header chrome only: macOS traffic-light circles on the left, Windows minimize/maximize/close on the right, Linux-style title/close header controls.
Preserve onboarding flow, IPC, persistence, recoverable retry, and stable data-testid selectors.
Update focused onboarding checks to assert platform detection plus chrome-only variance, not three full native skins.
out: No per-OS fonts, copy variants, body color tokens, radio skins, or statusline skins.
No redesign of Terminal, Mini, Pet, dashboard, or web gateway.
No changes to reward, tracker, or local-state schemas.

acceptance_criteria.summary: All platforms render the same terminal Welcome body: shared palette tokens, monospace stack, kitcode-setup tab content language, NORMAL statusline, and [x]/[ ] option marks.
Setup still resolves darwin/win32/linux, binds data-platform, and Electron passes platform into renderOnboardingWindow.
Header controls differ by OS only: macOS left traffic lights, Windows right window controls, Linux-style header controls; body styling does not branch per OS.
Auto-track, projects, companion choice, save/retry, and selectors behave as before the visual revert.
Reuse existing onboarding-platform chrome helpers and onboarding-window DOM/testids; do not fork a second Welcome app or invent unrelated design tokens outside the restored terminal palette.

coverage_plan.summary: Assert shared terminal markers, platform binding, and chrome class per OS without requiring three native body skins.
Keep pet/onboarding script assertions aligned with chrome markers.
Run the Linux-rendered setup interaction flow through headless Chromium with a mock bridge.
Re-run project registration and retry coverage unchanged.

risks.summary: Existing checks assert full per-OS themes and semantic token skins.
risks.mitigation: Narrow assertions to shared terminal UI plus chrome class / data-platform.

risks.summary: macOS Electron hiddenInset traffic lights may coexist with HTML chrome circles.
risks.mitigation: Keep current Electron chrome options; HTML lights stay decorative/aligned with left placement.

implementation_handoff.summary: Collapse onboarding-platform to detection + chrome fragments; restore terminal Welcome body in onboarding-window; keep Electron platform pass-through; update focused checks.
design_system_refs: Restored shared terminal palette (#050705 / #0b0f0c / #fc0a0a) and monospace stack in onboarding-window.mjs.
onboarding-platform.mjs now only owns resolveSetupPlatform, markers, and renderPlatformChrome.
Existing data-testid selectors and radiogroup interaction script preserved.
suggested_sequence: Slim onboarding-platform to platform id/marker/chromeClass + chrome HTML.
Restore terminal body HTML/CSS/JS in onboarding-window and inject platform chrome only.
Align Electron backgroundColor to terminal palette; keep platform window options.

verification.browser_evidence: Headless Chromium executed the Linux-rendered terminal Welcome flow: restored persisted NO, Arrow focus plus Space/Enter exclusive selection, appended and deduplicated two picker passes, removed only the scoped pending project, submitted autoTrack=false and companionView=pet, exposed recoverable RETRY SAVE, completed with SETUP COMPLETE, and had no body overflow.
environment_notes: Browser interaction expectations were updated for restored uppercase terminal copy (ADDED / RETRY SAVE / SETUP COMPLETE).
Per-OS visual chrome fidelity on real macOS, Windows, and Linux desktops remains a manual smoke check.
